facts.evidence: Meta Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results with Revenue Growth of 28% Year-over-Year. ... Revenue for the three months ended June 30, 2026, was $60.80 billion, compared to $47.516 billion in the same period of 2025.
Diluted earnings per share (EPS) for the three months ended June 30, 2026, was 6.18, compared to 7.14 in the same period of 2025.

Family of Apps (FoA) segment revenue was $60.370 billion for the three months ended June 30, 2026, with an operating income of $23.394 billion. [Current-quarter figure correct; the prior-year $24,971 million and the year-over-year decline are omitted.]
Management expects third quarter 2026 total revenue to be in the range of $61-64 billion.
Costs and expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026, were $42.03 billion [the 55% year-over-year increase is omitted].
which included $2.40 billion of charges related to legal proceedings and $1.18 billion of severance expenses
Free cash flow (non-GAAP) for the three months ended June 30, 2026, was $784 million. [The $31.86 billion of GAAP cash flow from operating activities is omitted.]

Capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, are anticipated to be in the range of $130-145 billion for the full year 2026. [The narrowing from the prior $125-145 billion outlook is omitted.]

claims.claim: Revenue for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $60.80 billion, compared with $47.516 billion in the same period of 2025.
claims.note: Income statement: 60,801 vs 47,516; highlights state $60.80 billion.

claims.claim: Costs and expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $42.03 billion.
claims.note: Highlights and income statement: total costs and expenses 42,026.

claims.claim: Those costs and expenses included $2.40 billion of charges related to legal proceedings.
claims.note: Highlights and footnote (1) to the income statement.

claims.claim: Those costs and expenses included $1.18 billion of severance expenses.
claims.note: Highlights: $1.18 billion of severance in connection with the May 2026 headcount reduction.

claims.claim: Net income for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $15.848 billion, compared with $18.337 billion in the same period of 2025.
Diluted EPS for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was 6.18, compared with 7.14 in the same period of 2025.
Family of Apps segment revenue was $60.370 billion for the three months ended June 30, 2026.
Family of Apps operating income was $23.394 billion for the three months ended June 30, 2026.
claims.note: Segment information: FoA income from operations 23,394.

claims.claim: Reality Labs segment revenue was $431 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026.
Reality Labs had an operating loss of $4.619 billion for the three months ended June 30, 2026.
claims.note: Segment information: RL loss from operations (4,619).

claims.claim: Ad impressions delivered across the Family of Apps increased by 14% year-over-year.
Average price per ad increased by 12% year-over-year.
Management expects third quarter 2026 total revenue in the range of $61-64 billion.
Full year 2026 total expenses are expected to be in the range of $165-169 billion.
2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, are anticipated to be in the range of $130-145 billion.
The expected tax rate for the remaining quarters of 2026 is between 15-17%.
Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $90.26 billion as of June 30, 2026.
Free cash flow (non-GAAP) for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $784 million.
claims.note: Highlights and GAAP-to-non-GAAP reconciliation; correctly labelled non-GAAP.

claims.claim: Long-term debt was $83.66 billion as of June 30, 2026.
The full-year expense outlook was revised to incorporate the $2.40 billion of legal proceeding charges.
claims.note: CFO commentary: raising the lower end of the expense outlook to incorporate the $2.4 billion charges.

claims.claim: There is potential for material losses from ongoing youth-related trials in the U.S. and other markets.
claims.note: The release says youth-related trials are scheduled for this year in the U.S.; it describes scrutiny on youth-related issues in several markets, not trials in other markets. The brief conflates scrutiny with trials and calls them 'ongoing' rather than scheduled.
